tapeLine: Monday 26 October closed higher: S&P 500 +0.70% (53.09 points) to 7,676.77, Nasdaq +0.82% to 26,169.38, Dow +0.28% (146.42 points) to 52,361.58, Russell 2000 +0.4% to 2,786.42, per the AP-style index recap (26 Oct). Tuesday futures levels were not confirmed; one report described them as mixed.
matters:
AI sentiment drove Monday’s rebound: reports tied the gains to Anthropic’s IPO filing lifting tech, with many parts of the market participating, per CNBC’s live coverage (26 Oct).

The Fed meets 27-28 October and is widely expected to hold rates; fed-funds futures priced only a 9.4% chance of a 25bp hike, per the same coverage. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report later this week.

Year to date through Monday: S&P 500 +12.1%, Nasdaq +12.6%, Dow +8.9%, Russell 2000 +12.3%, per the AP-style recap. Outlets differ by a few points on the Dow close.

Invalidation: the S&P 500 remains below Tuesday 20 October’s 7,712.57 close and about 1.7% under its 7,811.54 record close of 9 October; a close above 7,712.57 would reverse that read.
alsoOnTape: Gold and VIX levels were not found with a dated source and are not carried. Oil and 10-year yield figures appeared only in an undated secondary summary and are not carried.

regime.tag: Monday reversed Friday’s drop: all three indexes rose on AI sentiment, with the Nasdaq leading, while the S&P 500 stays below its 20 October close.
regime.sizing: The FOMC decision (28 October) and big-tech earnings later this week are the scheduled catalysts.

secondOrder: The driver flipped again: Friday’s pressure came from energy costs and hit the Dow; Monday’s relief came from AI sentiment and favoured the Nasdaq. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior brief’s invalidation level held: the S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,676.77, still below 7,712.57, per the 26 Oct recap.
The prior brief framed oil as the current driver (“a rotation of pressure”); Monday’s move was attributed to AI sentiment instead, with the Nasdaq leading and the Dow lagging.
Whether yields kept falling after the PPI print still cannot be graded: no dated, sourced yield levels were found.
The 27-28 October FOMC has not concluded; the decision is due 28 October.
